findings.question: Is the FLEX experiment table internally consistent with the per-test files?
findings.result: The PSI table's 'FLEX Test #' differs from official FLEX numbering for 119 of 274 rows (offset 1-6). Matching on the CIR identifier restores agreement: refitted K vs tabulated K r = 0.987 (n=206) versus r = 0.729 with the table numbering.
findings.dataset: PSI-69 experiment table, TestSheet and DropletData files; NASA/TP-2015-216046
findings.method: CIR-id join; OLS of d^2 vs t on 0.2-0.9 tb
findings.limitations: Tests without CIR id or with duplicate CIR id keep the table number.
findings.implication: Any reuse of the FLEX table must join on CIR id.
findings.feature: dataset integrity check; experiment lookup by official number

findings.question: Can the published FLEX burning-rate constants be reproduced from raw droplet histories?
findings.result: Yes: median difference -0.0011 mm^2/s, IQR [-0.0069, +0.0069] across 206 tests with R^2>0.95.
findings.method: OLS d^2 = a - K t on 0.2-0.9 of tabulated burn time
findings.uncertainty: Fit SE per test in flex_droplet_fits.csv
findings.limitations: Window choice affects K for short burns (tb < 2 s).
findings.implication: Tabulated K can be used with confidence once correctly keyed.

findings.question: How does K depend on O2 and diluent in FLEX?
findings.result: Per 0.1 increase in X_O2, K rises by 0.162 mm^2/s (methanol, 95% CI 0.142-0.183) and 0.192 mm^2/s (heptane, CI 0.117-0.257), holding pressure and diluent fixed. Helium vs N2 shift: methanol +0.144, heptane +0.144 mm^2/s.
findings.method: OLS with bootstrap (2000 resamples of tests)
findings.uncertainty: Bootstrap 95% CI; measurement error in K not reported
findings.limitations: Non-factorial design; droplet size pooled; descriptive model only.
findings.implication: Higher O2 increases burning rate of liquid fuels; He diluent does not slow burning.

findings.question: Does combustion stop when the visible flame goes out (FLEX-035)?
findings.result: No. After visible extinction at 8.9 s the droplet regresses at 0.419±0.003 mm^2/s versus 0.412±0.004 while burning (ratio 1.02); regression stalls about 27 s later. The FLEX report attributes this to cool-flame burning.
findings.dataset: PSI-69 FLEX-035 DropletData and LLUVData; NASA/TP-2015-216046 Fig. 39
findings.method: OLS on d^2 before/after tabulated extinction time
findings.uncertainty: Standard errors of fitted slopes; extinction time from table
findings.limitations: One test; cool flame inferred from literature, not measured here.
findings.implication: Optical flame-out is not a reliable end-of-event signal for hydrocarbon liquid fires in microgravity.

findings.question: Were Saffire-II samples 2-5 and 2-6 tested at the same flow?
findings.result: No. Telemetry gives 20.0 cm/s for 2-5 and 25.0 cm/s for 2-6 (table: 20 for both; NTRS: 25 for 2-6). Spread rates 2.1 and 2.6 mm/s.
findings.dataset: PSI-99 telemetry workbook; PSI-99 table; NTRS 20170008805
findings.conditions: Cygnus, ~22% O2, concurrent flow, cotton-fiberglass fabric 5 x 29 cm
findings.method: Mean of two anemometers over 120 s after ignition
findings.uncertainty: Anemometer SD within window <0.1 cm/s; inter-anemometer difference up to 3 cm/s (sample 2-9)
findings.limitations: Single sample per flow; no spread-rate uncertainty.
findings.implication: Use measured flow (25 cm/s) for 2-6 in any model validation.
findings.applicability: Concurrent spread over thin fabric in microgravity

findings.question: Did materials that burn in 1-g screening burn in microgravity Saffire-II?
findings.result: Silicone sheets 0.27 and 0.61 mm thick, which burn completely or partially in 1-g upward tests, did not propagate in Saffire-II at 20 cm/s and ~22% O2 (table: insignificant burn).
findings.limitations: One flow speed and O2 level; result may not hold at higher flow or O2.
findings.implication: For these conditions 1-g upward screening was conservative for silicone.

findings.question: What smoke particle sizes must spacecraft detectors see?
findings.result: SAME-R median arithmetic mean diameters: Kapton 0.11 µm, Lampwick 0.18 µm, Pyrell 0.30 µm, Silicone 0.36 µm, Teflon 0.17 µm.
findings.uncertainty: IQR per material in Table T07
findings.implication: Detectors must respond to sub-micrometre particles; particle size depends on material and transport time.

findings.question: Can detector alarm performance be inferred from SAME-R?
findings.result: Not from the PSI tables: the ISS scatter channel is at or above 6.2 V in 50% of 109 SAME-R tests, consistent with range saturation; no alarm thresholds or times are recorded.
findings.limitations: Saturation inferred from value clustering, not from instrument documentation.
findings.implication: AeroFox must not claim detector response times from these data.

findings.question: Do PSI solid-material tests cover exploration atmospheres?
findings.result: No PSI solid-fuel flight test lies within 10 kPa and 3 percentage points O2 of 56.5 kPa/34% or 66.2 kPa/28.5%; all Saffire and BASS-II tests were at ~101 kPa and <=22.2% O2. The closest liquid-fuel data are FLEX droplet tests near 72 kPa and X_O2 = 0.34, and ACME gaseous flames near 50-55 kPa with X_O2 0.3-0.4, which do not transfer to cabin solids.
findings.limitations: Literature-only data (e.g. ground NASA-STD-6001 tests) not included.
findings.implication: Lunar-habitat material decisions at elevated O2 need ground testing at the target atmosphere and SoFIE/FM2 results.

findings.question: Can lunar-gravity fire behaviour be interpolated between 1 g and microgravity?
findings.result: No. In simulated lunar gravity (LUCI) downward spread over SIBAL was 0.6x (flame base) and 0.39x (flame tip) the 1-g rate, while FM2 reports materials more flammable at lunar gravity than in 1 g.
findings.locator: LUCI combined results slide; FM2 abstract
findings.limitations: Short duration, rotating platform, Coriolis effects.
findings.implication: Treat lunar and Martian fire behaviour as unknown unless tested; do not interpolate.

findings.question: What drives radiative extinction of droplets?
findings.result: Extinction diameter as a fraction of initial diameter increases as X_O2 decreases (Spearman rho Heptane -0.49, Methanol -0.64).
findings.implication: Large fuel volumes in low O2 may self-extinguish early, but cool flames can persist.

findings.question: How much of the PSI combustion archive is analysis-ready?
findings.result: 66,567 catalog entries (13.50 TB). AeroFox's verified snapshot uses 40 MB: 22 experiment tables, 260 FLEX droplet histories, 272 FLEX test sheets, CFI files and reduced aerosol data.
findings.limitations: Video and image archives not analysed.
